name: Oldham

licensing.selective: Selective licensing in five designated areas covering parts of Alexandra, St Mary's, St James', Waterhead, Coldhurst, Werneth, Chadderton South, Hollinwood and Medlock Vale wards, from 4 July 2022 to 3 July 2027; the council's maps show the streets included. A wider scheme covering about 40% of the borough was consulted on in 2024; we could not confirm a decision.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme found; national mandatory HMO licensing (five or more people from two or more households) applies.
licensing.fee: £582 per selective licence, as stated on the council's site

housing: Oldham's inner areas, such as Coldhurst, Westwood, Werneth and Glodwick, are dominated by Victorian brick terraces built for the cotton mills, and this is where most private renting and the selective licensing areas are. Chadderton, Royton, Shaw and Failsworth mix terraces with inter-war semis and post-war estates. In the east, the Saddleworth villages on the edge of the Pennines are stone-built and largely owner-occupied. Private renting grew quickly between 2011 and 2021, and rents have risen sharply since.
checkinTips: Terraces inside the selective licensing areas: note the licence number and photograph smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, which are licence conditions.
Victorian terraces in Coldhurst, Werneth and Glodwick: photograph damp at the base of walls, cellar heads, back yards and alley gates.
Stone cottages in Saddleworth: photograph damp in thick walls, stoves and chimneys, and window frames exposed to Pennine weather.
Flats over shops in the town centre: record the separate entrance, stairs, fire doors and where the meters are.
Hillside terraces in Lees and Shaw: photograph steps, retaining walls, gutters and any damp in back rooms built into the slope.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Oldham Council's private sector housing team.
